original_value: Analyzing demand behavior of end consumers is pivotal in long term energy planning. Various models exist for simulating household load profiles to cater different purposes. A macroscopic viewpoint necessitates modeling of a large-scale population at an aggregate level, whereas a microscopic perspective requires measuring loads at a granular level, pertinent to the individual devices of a household. Both aspects lucrative benefits, instigating the need to combine them into a modeling framework which allows model scalability and flexibility, and to analyze domestic electricity consumption at different resolutions. In this applied research, we propose a multi-resolution agent-based modeling and simulation (ABMS) framework for estimating domestic electricity consumption. Our proposed framework simulates per minute electricity consumption by combining large neighborhoods, the behavior of household individuals, their interactions with the electrical appliances, their sociological habits and the effects of exogenous conditions such as weather and seasons. In comparison with the existing energy models, our framework uniquely provides a hierarchical, multi-scale, multi-resolution implementation using a multi-layer architecture. This allows the modelers flexibility in order to model large-scale neighborhoods at one end, without any loss of expressiveness in modeling microscopic details of individuals’ activities at house level, and energy consumption at the appliance level, at the other end. The validity of our framework is demonstrated using a case study of 264 houses. A validated ABMS framework will support: (a) Effective energy planning; (b) Estimation of the future energy demand; (c) and the analysis of the complex dynamic behavior of the consumers.

result.paraphrase: Understanding end-consumer demand behavior is essential for long-term energy planning. Household load profiles can be simulated with different models depending on the intended purpose. A macroscopic view models a large population in aggregate, while a microscopic view measures loads at a granular level, down to the individual devices in a household. Because both viewpoints offer valuable benefits, they should be combined in a framework that is scalable and flexible and that can analyze domestic electricity consumption at multiple resolutions. In this applied study, we present a multi-resolution agent-based modeling and simulation (ABMS) framework for estimating domestic electricity use. The framework generates per-minute electricity consumption by integrating large neighborhoods, household members’ behavior, their interactions with electrical appliances, sociological habits, and exogenous factors such as weather and seasons. Compared with existing energy models, it uniquely offers a hierarchical, multi-scale, multi-resolution implementation built on a multi-layer architecture. This gives modelers the flexibility to represent large-scale neighborhoods while still capturing microscopic details of individuals’ activities at the household level and appliance-level energy consumption. The framework’s validity is demonstrated through a case study of 264 houses. A validated ABMS framework will support: (a) effective energy planning; (b) estimation of future energy demand; and (c) analysis of the complex dynamic behavior of consumers.
